intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome (CLPED1) is caused by homozygous mutation in the NECTIN1 gene (600644) on chromosome 11q23.3. Heterozygosity for a NECTIN1 mutation has been associated with sporadic nonsyndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate (OFC7), which is included here.

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome (CLPED1) is caused by homozygous mutation in the NECTIN1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome is a rare, autosomal recessive disorder caused by homozygous loss-of-function mutations of the poliovirus receptor-like 1 (PVRL1) gene encoding nectin-1.
checks.explanation: PVRL1 is the former symbol for NECTIN1.

checks.claim: The NECTIN1 gene is located on chromosome 11q23.3.
checks.evidence_quote: which we identify as PVRL1, encoding nectin-1
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention 11q23.3. It counts as supported only under the rule that a gene's chromosomal location is standard nomenclature.

checks.claim: Heterozygosity for a NECTIN1 mutation has been associated with sporadic nonsyndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate (OFC7).
checks.evidence_quote: Here we demonstrate highly significant association between heterozygosity for this mutation and sporadic, non-syndromic CL/P in northern Venezuela.
checks.explanation: The paper states the association with heterozygosity. Using NECTIN1 and the OFC7 label only restates the paper's PVRL1 and CL/P.

(1998) described it as having unusual facies, dental anomalies, hypotrichosis, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and onychodysplasia, syndactyly, and cleft lip/cleft palate. Some affected individuals also have intellectual disability (Zlotogora et al., 1987; Rodini and Richieri-Costa, 1990).

paragraphs.text: Bustos et al. (1991) described 27 individuals from 7 families, very probably related to each other, who had ectodermal dysplasia and other anomalies with variable expressivity. The families came from a relatively isolated and inbred population on Margarita Island, Nueva Esparta State, in northeastern Venezuela. Females were affected as severely as males, and all parents were normal. The authors found that the clinical picture shared by all patients could not be classified among the known ectodermal dysplasias, and that previously published cases did not resemble their patients.

checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity for a nonsense mutation of PVRL1, W185X, results in an autosomal recessive CL/P syndrome on Margarita Island, CLPED1 (ref. 1).

paragraphs.text: In a 7-year-old Japanese boy with CLPED1 born to consanguineous parents, Yoshida et al. (2015) found a homozygous c.400C-T transition in exon 2 of the PVRL1 (NECTIN1) gene, resulting in an arg134-to-ter (R134X) substitution. Both parents were heterozygous for the mutation. The boy had hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia with sparse, brittle, fine, dry hair, as well as hypodontia, cleft lip/palate, cutaneous syndactyly of the fingers, and mild mental retardation. His hair showed pili torti and pili trianguli et canaliculi. The authors noted that the mutation is predicted to produce a truncated nectin-1 protein lacking the transmembrane and intracellular domains.
